registered: 2026-11-05, before any confirmatory data: only entries from 2026-11-06 on count; the 11 entries of 11/05 that suggested H2 are EXCLUDED (the hypothesis came from them)
operator: 2026-11-05 'pre-register fast %R rise of 30 or more over 5 minutes' (after VMRK; 4 of 5 never-greens today had a fast rise >= 30)
supersedes_partly: running list row 85 item (5): the flat-entry rule (H1) keeps its fixed definition but now shares the corrected bar with H2
question: Which, if either, of two %R slope reads at entry marks never-green desk entries?

hypotheses.H1_flat: flat = max(|wr_d5_fast|, |wr_d5_slow|) <= 10.7 marks never-green (fixed 11/04 before data; origin: sideways test 11/04, z +1.5, exploratory)
hypotheses.H2_steep: steep = wr_d5_fast >= 30.0 (fast %R line rose 30 or more points over the last 5 closed minutes) marks never-green (origin: 11/05, 5 never-greens vs 6 others, 4/5 vs 1/6 above 30; exploratory, n=11, post hoc; the closed 10/30 pitch study on 230,128 events found steep slow-pitch bands no worse than others, which argues against)

data: desk entries from 2026-11-06, features.wr_d5_fast / wr_d5_slow from ai_reports/outcomes.jsonl (ai_watch_wr_slope_log, live since 11/04 16:00); never-green = peak_price < entry +5 bp (hold-length dependent, stated limitation); net = (exit-entry)/entry bp - 3 bp
read_when: 150 forward entries with the slope fields; tools/studies/wr_slope_forward.py prints NOT DUE before that
multiple_comparisons: two hypotheses -> each needs pooled one-sided z >= 1.96 (p < 0.025)

pass_each.never_green: flagged-group never-green rate above the rest in BOTH halves (split by date at the median) and pooled z >= 1.96
pass_each.payoff: mean net of the unflagged group above the mean of all in both halves and the day-clustered bootstrap 5th percentile of (unflagged - all) > 0
pass_each.power: each half needs >= 40 flagged entries and >= 8 days, else UNDERPOWERED for that hypothesis
pass_each.confound: if rs_rng15_bp is present (range-position logger), the never-green gap must be positive in >= 2 of 3 range terciles

if_pass: skeptic review of the positive, then an observe-only flag in the Gates column, then a gate only through the sweep and ship-log rules; never straight to live
if_fail: close; no retuning of 10.7, 30.0, the 5-minute window or the label; record in the running list and memory
status: amended_1 after result-skeptic round 1 (NOT READY, 6 items); awaiting round 2; nothing scored

amended_1.threshold_origin: 30.0 is a POST HOC cutoff taken from the split of the 11 entries on 2026-11-05, not a pre-chosen round number; it is fixed now and will not be moved.
amended_1.start_pinned: confirmatory entries start 2026-11-06; 11/04 (logging began 16:00, sideways-test day) and 11/05 are excluded; the scorer ignores an earlier --since.
amended_1.no_peeking: the scorer may not be read for a verdict before the due date; the pre-due output is counts only.
amended_1.clustering: never-green inference is day-clustered: pass needs the day-bootstrap 2.5th percentile of (flagged - rest) never-green rate > 0 (one-sided 0.025, Bonferroni for two hypotheses) in addition to the pooled trade-level z >= 1.96 (shown for reference).
amended_1.label: rows with no peak_price are dropped and counted (a missing peak is not never-green). Because peak_price depends on hold length, the median hold by group is printed and the gap must also be positive among entries held >= 120 s; a fixed-horizon bar label is not available from outcomes and is listed as a limitation.
amended_1.power_and_extension: read when >= 150 entries AND the hypothesis has >= 60 flagged entries in total and >= 30 per half; otherwise UNDERPOWERED and re-read at every +50 entries until 400 entries, then close as UNDERPOWERED. At ~80 flagged vs ~70 rest, a pooled z of 1.96 needs a gap of about 20 percentage points; modest true effects will be missed.
amended_1.halves: split at the median ENTRY (by entry time), not the median day; each half needs >= 8 days.
amended_1.confound: if the range logger is absent or a tercile has < 5 flagged or rest entries, the verdict says 'range confound NOT TESTABLE' instead of passing silently; NaN z is UNDERPOWERED.

amended_feed.when: 2026-11-06 ~12:40 ET, before any SIP-period entry exists and before any of these tests was read (operator 'yes' to the SIP amendment).
amended_feed.why: The logged range, efficiency, run-size and slope measures come from the in-memory 1-minute bar store: IEX bars until the SIP flip (planned for the first SIP regular session, Tuesday 2026-11-10), SIP bars after. Denser SIP bars change what 'choppy' or 'top of range' reads as, so the two periods are not comparable.
amended_feed.rule: Entries are assigned to the IEX sample (entry time before docs/studies/feed_regime.json sip_from_et, or all entries while it is null) or the SIP sample (at or after it). The two samples are NEVER pooled. The test is read ONCE, on the first sample whose entry count reaches this prereg's minimum (ordered by entry time); the other sample is information only and does not change the verdict. All other rules (hypothesis, cuts computed on the read sample, bars, family size, extension rule) apply unchanged to the read sample.
amended_feed.flip_time: sip_from_et is set in the same step that flips alpaca_bar_feed to sip (docs/SIP_DAY1_RUNBOOK.md); tools/sip_sunday_check.py refuses GO while the feed is sip and it is null. If SIP is not bought or the flip slips, every entry stays in the IEX sample and the read is on IEX as originally written.
amended_feed.tool: tools/studies/feed_regime.py (shared), counts printed per sample nightly; tests/test_feed_regime.py.
